chunks: My father (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to us from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Isma'il ibn Marrar, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Ali ibn Abi Hamza, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed to Isa ibn Maryam (peace be upon him): O Isa! I have not honoured any creature with the like of My religion, nor have I bestowed upon it a blessing like My mercy. Wash with water what is apparent of you, and heal with good deeds what is hidden, for indeed you are returning to Me. Prepare yourself, for all that is coming is near. And let Me hear from you a sorrowful voice.

key_terms.أوحى: wahiy - divine revelation, specifically to prophets
key_terms.ديني: din - religion, the divinely prescribed way of life
key_terms.رحمتي: rahmah - mercy, divine compassion and grace
key_terms.شمر: shammara - to roll up one's sleeves, prepare oneself diligently

ai.seo_question: What did God reveal to Prophet Jesus (Isa) about religion and mercy in Islamic tradition?
ai.summary: In this hadith qudsi (divine saying), Imam al-Sadiq (AS) transmits a revelation from God to Prophet Isa (Jesus, AS). God reminds Isa that religion and divine mercy are the greatest gifts bestowed upon creation, and instructs him to purify both the outward self through ritual ablution and the inward self through good deeds. The exhortation to prepare and weep before God reflects the theme of spiritual readiness for the return to the Hereafter, a common instruction given to prophets in Islamic tradition.
word_analysis: may He have mercy on him
